title: Requirements Engineering & Scope & Prioritisation
goal: Turn the opportunity brief into a requirement set that says what must change for the business, what each stakeholder needs and what the system must do and how well — traceable and testable. Decide what is in, out and later, break the initiative into epics and features, slice them for early value and learning, and put them in one order by economic value.
story: The idea got a Go. Now you decide exactly what to build first and why: the requirements, what's in and out, how big it is, the release plan, and the go-ahead to invest. In the example: release one reads clean PDFs automatically; tricky orders come later.

I'm working through "Define MVP & Scope Boundary" (Plan → Scope & Prioritisation) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Decide the smallest scope that proves the value hypothesis, and say plainly what is out.
Done looks like: A scope statement: the MVP, in / out / later lists with reasons, and the hypothesis the MVP tests.

I'll attach or paste: Requirements baseline; Opportunity brief.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Map the journey as a story map → Story map
2. Draw the MVP line → MVP definition
3. List in / out / later with reasons → In / out / later list
4. MVP tests the hypothesis end to end? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
5. Publish the scope statement → Scope statement

Produce: Story map; Scope statement. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: MVP tests the value hypothesis end to end; Every out item has a reason; End to end.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

definition.purpose: Cut features into thin vertical slices so value and learning arrive early and risk falls fast.
definition.outcome: A slice plan: each feature cut into valuable, demonstrable, independently testable slices, with a walking skeleton first.
definition.jtbd: Help me get something real in front of users soon, and learn the risky bits first.

Apply splitting patterns to each feature

exceptions: Slice still too big → split by business-rule variation or by data type

criteria: Valuable, demonstrable, independently testable, small enough

policies: Slices sized to fit well inside one sprint

decisions: Which slice goes first

execution.authority: Product owner accepts the slice plan; the architect rules on slices that need design decisions.

lessons.title: Order by Value (WSJF)
lessons.summary: Score cost of delay against size and put the backlog in one agreed order.

definition.purpose: Put the backlog in one order, by economic value and risk, so the team always works on the most valuable next thing.
definition.outcome: An ordered product backlog with WSJF scores and rationale, dependencies respected and the order agreed.
definition.jtbd: Help me defend why this comes before that — with numbers, not volume.
exit: Every now-horizon item scored and ranked
No two items share a rank
Sponsor and product owner agree the order

normal: Score cost of delay: user and business value, time criticality, risk reduction
Take job size from Estimation (or a provisional size)

cases.happyPath: Scores separate clearly and the order is accepted.
alternates: Regulatory or contractual date → time criticality dominates
edgeCases: Two items tie
An enabler with no direct user value
exceptions: A stakeholder lobbies for a pet item → score it in the open
failures: Ordered by the most senior voice

routing.forward: → 2.3 Estimation & Capacity (sizes refine the order) and 2.4 Roadmap
routing.alternate: Enabler ranked by the risk it retires
routing.escalation: Ordering dispute between stakeholders → sponsor; between initiatives → portfolio board
routing.stop: Item scores near zero on every factor → move to later or remove — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Relative scales (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 20)
Scored by a group, not one person
rules: One ordered list — no parallel 'priority 1' lists
policies: Order reviewed at every roadmap review

decisions: Backlog order

roles: C — Sponsor, Engineering lead, Finance partner
execution.authority: Product owner orders the backlog; sponsor breaks disputes; portfolio board ranks across initiatives.

continuity.handoff: Ordered product backlog and WSJF scoring sheet → 2.3 Estimation & Capacity and 2.4.1 Map Dependencies & Constraints
traceability: WSJF score recorded on each FEA-###
continuity.timebox: ½–1 day, then at every roadmap review
